task.goal: Some boxes leave filling out of spec. Ship only good ones. Score: a 90 s production run must ship at least 29 good items per minute to the shipping bin, with at most 0 bad boxes shipped, no spills and no jams. You have $1550 for parts.

params.title: Plant 1017
params.rules:
A factory floor of square cells, 0.5 m each; x grows east, y grows north. Items (boxes, 14 cm
cubes, unless the task says the line makes toys) arrive from inlets (I) and must end up in the shipping bin (G). Map symbols: > < ^ v belts (arrow = flow),
W scale, P pusher, R reject bin, # wall, . empty.
Parts (price): belt $20 (speed m/s); scale $400 (a belt section with a load cell; boxes
whose reading is below reject_below_g or above reject_above_g are flagged); pusher $300 (stands
beside a belt and pushes across it in its direction; fires when a flagged box is offset_mm before the paddle
line, stays out stroke_ms); reject bin $60. Removing a part refunds half its price.
Belts carry boxes by friction: boxes need time to speed up or turn, so fast turns, merges and drop-offs can
throw boxes. Rails are fitted automatically on belt edges nothing feeds into, except the side a pusher pushes
through. A box falling to the floor is a spill. A box that sits still on a belt for 3 s is a jam. Bins
stand on platform scales: runs report each bin's count and total weight. A good box weighs about
1.00 kg (toys less); other items may be underfilled or double-packed.
Build language (one command per line; X or Y may be a range like 2..5):
  belt X Y DIR speed=<m/s>          DIR is E, W, N or S
  scale X Y DIR speed=<m/s> reject_below_g=<g> reject_above_g=<g>
  pusher X Y DIR offset_mm=<mm> stroke_ms=<ms>
  bin X Y
  set X Y key=value ...           retune a placed part
  remove X Y
